slides.texte_overlay:
Things your 30-year-old self
will thank you for
Learning to cook ten real meals. Healthier, cheaper, and you'll never panic when friends come over. It's one of the most useful skills you can build early.
Starting to save, even a little. A small amount every month in your 20s grows into real security by 30, and money stress disappears from your life.
Taking care of your teeth, your skin and your back. Dentist, sunscreen, stretching. Small habits now save you a lot of pain and money ten years later.
Keeping the friends who make you better. Fewer, deeper friendships with people who push you and support you will matter far more than any big group.
Building a learning habit. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and ten years of tiny lessons will add up to a very different, sharper man.
slides.texte_sophia: Building a learning habit. I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Ten years of tiny lessons will add up to a very different man.

slides.texte_overlay: Training your body regularly. Not for summer, for life. Strength and fitness built in your 20s make every decade after it easier and more enjoyable.
Travelling while it's cheap and easy. Hostels, trains, last-minute trips. The memories and the confidence you gain are worth far more than the money.
